title: Add bug-evidence default and criterion for bug requests
summary: Add a "bug-evidence" default to defaults.toml for bug, wrong-output and regression requests, and make the reader's pipeline ensure such a reading carries a criterion that the change names the root cause, shows it from readable data, and shows why the symptom follows, before any fix. Add a test that a bug request's reading gets the criterion. Audience: the verifier who rejects data-less root-cause claims at the final verdict.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the criterion and the default; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The criterion is added by code in the reading builder rather than left to prose.
The cause is that readings for bug requests carried no criterion demanding data-backed root-cause evidence.
Criteria run tests that show the reading gains the criterion.
One default plus one builder step.
The default and criterion text are plain for an outside reader.
The criterion text must be clear to a newcomer reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs build_reading (about line 685-848) builds the Reading from reader output and already calls ensure_changelog (line 281) to add a deliverable and a defaults_applied entry mechanically; crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses defaults.toml (REPO_DEFAULTS) and render() shows only each default's first sentence; no record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not touched.

Design: add a new default id `bug-evidence` (applies_to ["*"], source cites the four introspections) whose first sentence is short, rather than editing `root-cause`, whose text already says to fix the root cause. Add an analogous mechanical step beside ensure_changelog that, for a change reading from a bug, wrong-output, regression or slowdown request, appends the root-cause-evidence criterion and a defaults_applied entry once. The request keyword detection must be simple and tested.

The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom, so the new default's rendered line may overflow its 2000-token budget; the producer keeps the first sentence minimal and, only if the budget check fails, raises the reader budget in athena.toml.
The cited file records/failure-classes/2026-11/20261104-054711-kb90.json is evidence only and records/ never changes.
Existing tests must keep passing, including defaults.rs tests that assert rendered lines; no unrelated behavior changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] `bug-evidence` applying to bug, wrong-output and regression requests. It requires that the change names the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, code path, a failing case) and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows, before any fix. It says a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet it, and it cites the four introspection ids in its source.

The reading builder in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs adds the root-cause-evidence criterion and a defaults_applied entry exactly once for bug, wrong-output, regression and slowdown requests, and adds nothing for other requests.

A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a reading from a bug request and asserts the criterion is present. A second test asserts a non-bug request gets none and that running the step twice adds it once. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` to check.
A defaults.rs test asserts the `bug-evidence` default parses from the repo defaults.toml and its first-sentence line renders. Run `cargo test -p athena-data` to check.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` pass across the workspace, with existing tests unchanged in outcome and prompt token budgets still within limits.
Governance files: defaults.toml is changed and named here. athena.toml changes only if the reader prompt budget check requires it, and then only that budget value.

Standing defaults hold. outcome-check: a newcomer reading the new default and the criterion text understands what evidence is required. root-cause: the change description names why bug jobs were being rejected. no-empty-success and thrash-stop apply unchanged.

out_of_scope: Changing records/ or any owner file, including records/failure-classes/2026-11/20261104-054711-kb90.json
Changing the verifier's final-verdict rejection logic
Fixing the individual bug and slowdown jobs that were rejected
departures: The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom, so the new default's rendered line may need a budget change, which adds some risk and cost.
urgent_reason: It cuts rejected attempts: bug and slowdown jobs were rejected at the final verdict in 3 jobs for lacking a data-backed root cause.
hard_reason: It adds a rule that can reject jobs at the final verdict and changes how a reading is built in the run pipeline.
